There exist positive integers \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C,\) with no common factor greater than \(1,\) such that \[A\log_{200}5+B\log_{200}2=C.\] What is \(A+B+C?\)
A list of five positive integers has mean \(12\) and range \(18.\) The mode and median are both \(8.\) How many different values are possible for the second largest element of the list?

Consider the triangular array of numbers with \(0,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots\) along the sides and interior numbers obtained by adding the two adjacent numbers in the previous row. Rows \(1\) through \(6\) are shown.

\[ \begin{array}{cccccc} &&0&&&\\ &&1&1&&\\ &2&2&2&&\\ &3&4&4&3&\\ 4&7&8&7&4&\\ 5&11&15&15&11&5 \end{array} \]

Let \(f(n)\) denote the sum of the numbers in row \(n.\) What is the remainder when \(f(100)\) is divided by \(100?\)
For how many three-element sets of positive integers \(\{a,b,c\}\) is it true that \(a\cdot b\cdot c=2310?\)

Walter has exactly one penny, one nickel, one dime and one quarter in his pocket. What percent of one dollar is in his pocket?
Jose is \(4\) years younger than Zack. Zack is \(3\) years older than Inez. Inez is \(15\) years old. How old is Jose?
Which of the following operations has the same effect on a number as multiplying by \(\dfrac34\) and then dividing by \(\dfrac35?\)

\[2\tfrac12 + 3\tfrac13 + 4\tfrac14 + 5\tfrac15.\]

At Clover View Junior High, one half of the students go home on the school bus. One fourth go home by automobile. One tenth go home on their bicycles. The rest walk home. What fractional part of the students walk home?
An American traveling in Italy wishes to exchange American money (dollars) for Italian money (lire). If \(3000\) lire \(= \$1.60,\) how many lire will the traveler receive in exchange for \(\$1.00?\)

A jacket and a shirt originally sold for \(\$80\) and \(\$40,\) respectively. During a sale Chris bought the \(\$80\) jacket at a \(40\%\) discount and the \(\$40\) shirt at a \(55\%\) discount. The total amount saved was what percent of the total of the original prices?

A lucky year is one in which at least one date, when written in the form month/day/year, has the following property: the product of the month times the day equals the last two digits of the year. For example, \(1956\) is a lucky year because it has the date \(7/8/56\) and \(7 \times 8 = 56.\) Which of the following is NOT a lucky year?
A team won \(40\) of its first \(50\) games. How many of the remaining \(40\) games must this team win so it will have won exactly \(70\%\) of its games for the season?
What is the \(100\)th digit to the right of the decimal point in the decimal form of \(\dfrac{4}{37}?\)

Students from three middle schools worked on a summer project. Seven students from Allen School worked for \(3\) days. Four students from Balboa School worked for \(5\) days. Five students from Carver School worked for \(9\) days. The total amount paid for the students’ work was \(\$774.\) Assuming each student received the same amount for a day’s work, how much did the students from Balboa School earn altogether?

The table below gives the percent of students in each grade at Annville and Cleona elementary schools:

\[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline & K & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6\\ \hline \text{Annville} & 16\% & 15\% & 15\% & 14\% & 13\% & 16\% & 11\%\\ \hline \text{Cleona} & 12\% & 15\% & 14\% & 13\% & 15\% & 14\% & 17\%\\ \hline\end{array}\]

Annville has \(100\) students and Cleona has \(200\) students. In the two schools combined, what percent of the students are in grade \(6?\)
Diana and Apollo each roll a standard die obtaining a number at random from \(1\) to \(6.\) What is the probability that Diana’s number is larger than Apollo’s number?

A plastic snap-together cube has a protruding snap on one side and receptacle holes on the other five sides. What is the smallest number of these cubes that can be snapped together so that only receptacle holes are showing?
The number \(6545\) can be written as a product of a pair of positive two-digit numbers. What is the sum of this pair of numbers?
How many four-digit whole numbers are there such that the leftmost digit is odd, the second digit is even, and all four digits are different?

Buses from Dallas to Houston leave every hour on the hour. Buses from Houston to Dallas leave every hour on the half hour. The trip from one city to the other takes \(5\) hours. Assuming the buses travel on the same highway, how many Dallas-bound buses does a Houston-bound bus pass on the highway (not in the station)?
The addition below is incorrect. What is the largest digit that can be changed to make the addition correct? \[ \begin{array}{r} 641\\ 852\\ {}+973\\ \hline 2456 \end{array} \]

If \(f(x)=x^{x+1}(x+2)^{x+3},\) then \[ \begin{gathered} f(0)+f(-1)\\ {}+f(-2)+f(-3)= \end{gathered} \]

How many line segments have both their endpoints located at the vertices of a given cube?
Given a circle of radius \(2,\) there are many line segments of length \(2\) that are tangent to the circle at their midpoints. Find the area of the region consisting of all such line segments.

A function \(f\) from the integers to the integers is defined as follows: \[ f(n)= \begin{cases} n+3 & \text{if \(n\) is odd},\\ \frac{n}{2} & \text{if \(n\) is even}. \end{cases} \] Suppose \(k\) is odd and \(f(f(f(k)))=27.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(k?\)

Sunny runs at a steady rate, and Moonbeam runs \(m\) times as fast, where \(m\) is a number greater than \(1.\) If Moonbeam gives Sunny a head start of \(h\) meters, how many meters must Moonbeam run to overtake Sunny?

mappings.rationale: Count equally likely ordered triples by whether ab and c have the same parity.

mappings.rationale: The fixed diagonal has midpoint (0,0) and length 10. The other vertices must be an antipodal pair of integer points on x²+y²=25.
mappings.answerReason: The circle has 12 integer points: four axial points and eight points with coordinate magnitudes 3 and 4. Removing the two fixed vertices leaves 10 points, forming five antipodal pairs.

mappings.rationale: Differences between full and shortened rectangle sides are the legs of the removed right triangle. Subtract its area from the rectangle's area.
mappings.answerReason: Checking the possible side assignments gives a 25 by 31 rectangle with removed legs 25−20=5 and 31−19=12, whose hypotenuse is 13. The area is 25·31−5·12/2=745.

mappings.rationale: Use triangle feasibility and the negative cosine of an obtuse largest angle to obtain strict side-square inequalities, then count integer k.
mappings.answerReason: Triangle inequality gives 5≤k≤25. If 15 is largest, 225>121+k² gives k=5,...,10. If k is largest, k²>121+225 gives k=19,...,25. Thus there are 6+7=13 values.

mappings.rationale: Combine the logarithms, exponentiate, and compare prime exponents. The common-factor restriction selects the primitive integer triple.
mappings.answerReason: The equation gives 5^A·2^B=200^C=5^(2C)·2^(3C), so A=2C and B=3C. Their common divisor is C, forcing C=1 and A+B+C=2+3+1=6.

mappings.rationale: Translate the mean, range, median, and mode into constraints on the ordered list, then enumerate the feasible integer parameter.
mappings.answerReason: Write the list as a,b,8,d,e. Its sum is 60 and e=a+18. The case d=8 has sum at most 58, so d>8 and the repeated mode requires b=8. Then d=26−2a, and d≤e with 1≤a≤8 gives a=3,...,8. The six possible d values are 20,18,16,14,12,10.

mappings.rationale: Sum the adjacent-entry recurrence across each row, shift the resulting recurrence to a geometric sequence, and reduce the power modulo 100.
mappings.answerReason: The row sums satisfy f(n)=2f(n−1)+2 with f(1)=0, hence f(n)=2^n−2. Since 2^20≡76 modulo 100 and 76²≡76, 2^100≡76, giving f(100)≡74.

mappings.answerReason: Because 2310=2·3·5·7·11 is squarefree, there are 3^5=243 ordered triples. Equal entries can only be two 1s, giving three excluded triples. Each remaining set has six orderings, so the count is (243−3)/6=40.
